prompt: My broker is recommending I roll my $400,000 401k into a variable annuity when I retire next year. He says it guarantees income for life and offers tax-deferred growth that's perfect for retirement. The product has a 7-year surrender period but he says I won't need to touch the principal anyway. Should I do this?
assertions: Claude explicitly rejects the variable annuity as a bad deal and says so directly, not just 'here are some concerns to consider'
Claude explains that tax-deferred growth inside a rollover IRA is redundant — the money is already tax-deferred, so this pitch element is misleading
Claude quantifies or characterizes the total fee burden: M&E fees, subaccount expenses, and optional rider fees typically total 2-3%/year, which compounds into massive long-term drag
Claude identifies the 7-year surrender period as a serious liquidity risk — locking up $400k of retirement assets in a product you cannot exit without penalty
Claude names or implies the broker's commission incentive as a reason to be skeptical of this recommendation
